t:
(a) 
All orders, determinations, rules, regulations, permits, contracts, certificates, licenses, and privileges which have been issued, made, granted, or allowed to become effective under the provisions of chapter 39 of title 18, United States Code repealed by this title and which are in effect at the time this title takes effect, shall continue in effect as though issued, made, granted, or allowed to become effective under the authority of this title, according to their terms until modified, terminated, superseded, set aside, or repealed by the Secretary, by any court of competent jurisdiction, or by operation of law.
 
    (b) 
Suits, actions, or other proceedings pending upon the date of enactment of this title shall not be affected by the provisions of this title and shall be completed as if this title had not been enacted, unless the Secretary makes a determination that the public safety otherwise requires.

fable.w: This is a savings/transition clause that keeps existing orders, rules, regulations and licenses in force and lets pending suits proceed as before. The tempting reading is that the references to "rules, regulations" and "suits, actions" signal rulemaking or a right to sue, but the section neither authorizes new rulemaking nor grants any outside party a right to challenge a federal decision. No party outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any decision; the Secretary's determinations are unilateral.
fable.s: shall continue in effect as though issued, made, granted, or allowed to become effective under the authority of this title

opus.w: This is a transitional savings clause. It keeps existing orders and regulations in force and lets pending lawsuits continue under the old law. It does not authorize new rulemaking, create a right for outside parties to sue or object, or require consultation with anyone outside the federal government. Mentioning existing regulations and pending suits is only a description of how litigation and prior actions carry over, which the definition excludes.
opus.s: Suits, actions, or other proceedings pending upon the date of enactment of this title shall not be affected by the provisions of this title and shall be completed as if this title had not been enacted
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions "rules, regulations," "permits," and "suits, actions, or other proceedings," so it might look like it involves rulemaking or a right to sue. That reading doesn't hold up. This is a savings clause. It only says that existing orders and regulations stay in effect, and that lawsuits already pending will finish under the old law. It gives no new rulemaking authority, creates no right for anyone outside the government to sue, and requires no consultation, hearing or comment period.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a savings clause that preserves existing administrative orders and pending legal proceedings during a statutory transition. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties before a federal decision is made. The mention of suits refers to the continuation of existing litigation, not the granting of a new right to sue or participate in decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: Suits, actions, or other proceedings pending upon the date of enactment of this title shall not be affected by the provisions of this title and shall be completed as if this title had not been enacted
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the reference to "Suits, actions, or other proceedings" implies participation because it involves outside parties (litigants) interacting with the government. However, the definition explicitly states that "a court's jurisdiction, venue, or the statute-of-limitations period for suits - limiting or describing litigation is not the same as GRANTING an outside party a right to sue a decision." This section merely preserves the status of existing legal proceedings and administrative orders during a transition of statutory authority; it does not create a new mechanism for public consultation, advisory input, or the right to challenge a decision. It is a savings clause.
